To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the direct differentiation method for the sensitivity analysis of finite strain elasto-plasticity in indentation testing is suitable for parameter identification in indentation tests with flexible indenters.

the corotational finite element method is well-suited for sensitivity analysis and parameter identification, and that parameter identification in indentation experiments is sensitive to the load history.

(i) a corotational formulation can be used for sensitivity analysis of finite strain finite element simulations, (ii) the derivatives obtained by the direct differentiation method are in very good agreement with the results obtained by the use of the finite difference method, and (iii) the use of the direct differentiation method for sensitivity analysis in finite element simulations is a powerful tool for material parameter identification in the case of indentation testing.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of material parameters for finite strain elastically-plastic material behaviour using a gradient-based optimization procedure.
the development and application of a sensitivity analysis for finite strain elastically-plastically-deforming bodies.
the development and assessment of a methodology to determine material parameters from indentation data using finite strain elasto-plasticity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, for the case considered here, the optimization method works well for parameter identification, provided that the initial values of the parameters are close to the true ones.
the optimization-based parameter identification is very sensitive to artificial noise and that the load history is of minor influence on parameter identification in indentation.
parameter identification in indentation experiments is possible with the method presented.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the direct differentiation approach for the sensitivity analysis is suitable for the parameter identification of finite strain elasto-plastic material behaviour in indentation testing.
parameter identification in finite strain elasto-plasticity is feasible using the direct differentiation approach in a corotational formulation.
the direct differentiation method can be successfully applied to the case of finite strain finite element simulations of flexible-to-flexive contact.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the corotational approach is suitable for the sensitivity analysis and the identification of material parameters.
the corotational approach is well suited for the calculation of the derivatives in sensitivity analysis and parameter identification for finite element simulations of finite strain plasticity.
parameter identification in finite strain elasto-plasticity is possible with the use of the corotated formulation in sensitivity analysis and the direct differentiation method.
